projects.name: NN Playground
projects.description: A from-scratch, zero-dependency neural network engine (dense layers, backprop, SGD, tanh/relu/sigmoid) written in ~150 lines of plain JavaScript, with no libraries and no build step for the app itself. Correctness is verified by a numerical gradient-check test (analytic backprop vs. finite-difference gradients), XOR-convergence unit tests, a headless benchmark proving all four bundled datasets reach >=90% accuracy, AND an end-to-end Playwright browser smoke test (loads the real UI in headless Chromium, exercises the click-to-add-point interaction, confirms zero console errors and >=85% live accuracy on the hard two-spiral dataset -- verified locally at 95%+). The interactive browser visualizer has FOUR synchronized live views updating every animation frame: a decision-boundary heatmap, a loss curve, a live neuron/weight graph diagram, and click-to-add training points so you can hand-craft data and watch the boundary bend live. Includes a README screenshot of the converged spiral fit.
projects.runInstructions: No install needed for the core app. Open nn-playground/index.html directly in any modern browser (or serve the folder, e.g. `npx serve nn-playground`, if your browser blocks local file:// script loading). Pick a dataset, hidden-layer architecture, and learning rate; Play/Pause and Reset control the training loop; click/right-click the main canvas to add your own training points live. To run unit tests (incl. gradient check): `cd nn-playground && npm test`. Headless convergence benchmark: `npm run benchmark`. Optional real-browser end-to-end check: `npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium && npm run smoke`.
projects.testCommand: cd nn-playground && npm test && npm run benchmark

projects.name: Pathfinding & Maze Visualizer
projects.description: Interactive, dependency-free pathfinding & maze-generation visualizer. Draw walls, paint weighted "mud" terrain (right-click/shift-click), drag start/end nodes, generate a guaranteed-solvable random maze (recursive backtracker), and watch BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, A* (weight-aware), and Bidirectional BFS (grows frontiers from both ends, meets in the middle, visibly visits far fewer nodes) explore the grid live with stats (nodes visited, path length, path cost, runtime). A "Compare All Algorithms" mode races all 5 at once and renders a results table with the best values highlighted. Core algorithms live in a single shared vanilla-JS module (algorithms.js) used by both the browser UI and a zero-dependency Node test suite (12 passing unit tests). No build step, no npm install required to run the UI.
projects.runInstructions:
1. Open project/index.html directly in any modern browser (double-click, or `python3 -m http.server 8000` from the project/ dir and visit localhost:8000). No install needed.
2. Pick an algorithm (A*, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, Bidirectional BFS) from the dropdown, or click "Compare All" to race all 5 at once and see a results table.
3. Click "Generate Maze" for an instant solvable maze, or click/drag on the grid to draw walls; right-click/shift-click to paint weighted "mud" terrain; drag the green/red cells to move start/end.
4. Click "Visualize" to watch it search and reveal the path, with live stats below the grid.

To run tests: `cd project && npm test` (or `node test.js`) — expects "12 passed, 0 failed".

projects.name: Nebula — Barnes-Hut Galaxy Simulator
projects.description: A real-time N-body gravity simulator running entirely in the browser (vanilla JS + Canvas2D, zero dependencies, zero build step, zero server required — just double-click index.html). Implements a genuine Barnes-Hut quadtree approximation algorithm (O(n log n) instead of O(n²)) so it can simulate hundreds of mutually-gravitating bodies at a steady 60fps — and lets you watch the actual quadtree subdivide live via a toggleable overlay (see screenshots in the README). Overlapping bodies merge through momentum-conserving accretion, so simulated galaxies visibly clump into fewer, bigger bodies over time. Includes a seeded procedural spiral-galaxy generator, a random cluster mode, and a binary-star system mode, plus interactive controls (body count, simulation speed, θ accuracy/performance tradeoff, trails, quadtree overlay, collision toggle, zoom, and click-drag to fling new bodies with realistic velocity). The physics core is a pure, dependency-free ES module (physics.mjs) shared conceptually with a classic-script build (physics.inline.js) for zero-setup browser use, validated by a 20-test Node suite (test.mjs) covering Newton's third law, Barnes-Hut vs brute-force accuracy, quadtree mass conservation, momentum conservation across 200 integration steps, orbital energy-drift bounds, quadtree bounds extraction, and collision-merge conservation laws. Verified end-to-end with headless-browser smoke tests (Playwright) exercising every UI control with zero console/runtime errors.
projects.runInstructions:
Zero setup: just open `index.html` directly in a browser (double-click it, or `open index.html` / `xdg-open index.html`). No server, no build, no install — it uses a classic (non-module) script so it works over file:// with no CORS restrictions.

Click "Spiral Galaxy" / "Random Cluster" / "Binary System" to load a scene. Drag on the canvas to fling in new massive bodies (drag distance/direction sets velocity). Scroll to zoom. Toggle "Show Barnes-Hut tree" to see the actual quadtree used for physics subdividing live. Toggle "Collisions merge" to see momentum-conserving accretion. Use the sliders to change body count, simulation speed, and the Barnes-Hut θ accuracy/performance tradeoff live. See screenshot.png and screenshot-quadtree.png in the repo for a preview.

To run the automated physics test suite (Node, no browser needed):
`node test.mjs`
Expected output: `20 passed, 0 failed`.

projects.name: PyCrawler
projects.description: A procedurally generated ASCII roguelike dungeon crawler in pure Python 3, zero runtime dependencies. Dungeons are built with real Binary Space Partitioning (BSP): rooms carved in leaf nodes of a randomly split tree, corridors carved along the tree so every room is guaranteed reachable (verified by a flood-fill test across 25 seeds). Turn-based combat, monsters that chase on sight, items (potions/weapons/scrolls), fog-of-war with explored-tile memory, multi-level descent to a win condition, permadeath. Ships with a BFS-pathfinding heuristic bot that can autoplay full games headlessly (fight-adjacent -> grab loot -> hunt visible monsters -> beeline for stairs -> flee when critical), which doubles as both a no-TTY demo mode for judges/CI and an automated playthrough test. A real interactive curses UI is available for humans in a terminal. For browser-based judging with zero setup, tools/export_replay.py exports any autoplayed run to a single self-contained HTML file with an embedded play/pause/step/scrub replay viewer (no server, no network needed) -- two pre-generated examples (a win and a loss) ship in demos/. 11 pytest tests cover dungeon connectivity/determinism, game logic, and full win/lose playthroughs.
projects.runInstructions:
cd pycrawler
python3 -m pytest -q                                            # run the 11-test suite

# Easiest: open a pre-generated browser replay, no setup needed
open demos/replay_victory_seed3.html    # or: xdg-open / double-click in a file browser

# Generate a fresh browser replay for any seed:
python3 tools/export_replay.py --seed 7 --depth 3 --out replay.html && open replay.html

# Headless terminal demo (no TTY needed, prints every turn):
python3 -m pycrawler --demo --seed 3 --depth 3

# Interactive curses UI in a real terminal (WASD/arrows, u=use item, q=quit):
python3 -m pycrawler --play

Requires only Python 3.10+ stdlib (curses is stdlib; only needed for --play; the HTML replay viewer needs only a browser).
